title: How to strip floss for cross-stitch
subtitle: Separating the strands for a smooth, even stitch
excerpt: Cross-stitch floss is six strands twisted together. For most 14-count Aida work, two strands are needed. Stripping means separating the exact number of strands one at a time, then rethreading them together. This removes the twist and gives a smooth, flat stitch.
sourceNotes: Strand-stripping practice documented in Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), Project Gutenberg #20776. Standard practice consistent across all major cross-stitch teaching resources.

glossaryTerms.definition: The process of separating individual strands from a six-strand skein of embroidery floss. Each strand is pulled out one at a time, then the required number of strands are rethreaded together through the needle eye. Stripping removes the twist and produces a flatter, more even stitch.

content.text: Embroidery floss arrives as six strands twisted together. For 14-count Aida, two strands are the standard for the cross-stitch fill and one strand for the back-stitch outline.

means pulling the strands apart individually and then threading the required number together. Threading two stripped strands through the needle gives a flatter, more uniform stitch than cutting two-sixths of an un-stripped skein.
Cut a length of floss of about forty-five to fifty centimetres. Longer threads tangle and fray before they are used up; shorter threads run out too quickly.
Hold the bundle loosely and pull one strand straight up.

Hold all six strands at the top between finger and thumb. Grip one single strand at the very top and pull it straight upward while letting the other five hang below. The other strands will bunch as the single strand moves; this is normal.
Let the bundle drop and settle.
Once the single strand is free, let the remaining five strands hang and shake gently. They will untwist and hang straight. Repeat to remove each strand you need.
Lay the stripped strands side by side and thread together.

Place two stripped strands side by side with no twist between them. Thread both through the needle eye together. The two separate strands thread through as one unit and will lie flat side by side in each stitch.
, one to two strands for back-stitch.
14-count Aida: two strands for the fill, one strand for back-stitch.
16-count Aida: two strands for the fill, one strand for back-stitch.
18-count Aida or 28-count evenweave: one strand for the fill and one strand for back-stitch.
